description: [S7.2, kind `scope`] The exe class that Display::createWindow 0x100657e0 stores in g_listener 0x1012872c, whose vtable slots 0..10 jgld's window procedure calls (slot 5 mouse move, 7 left press with a double-click flag, 8 left release, 9 right press, 10 right release, 4 character, 3 key, see c3cd_notes.txt), is not identified. The message -> root-handler mapping in port/app/input_map.cpp is MEASURED on 26,861 corpus MSG records (every one of the 23,432 HANDLER records reproduced), not read from the listener's own code, so a message class the corpus lacks (U-1612..U-1614) has no static evidence either.
path to resolution: Find the argument of Display::createWindow's caller in the exe (pointer_callers.py on the createWindow slot of Display vtable 0x1011d640 gives the installer), name the class and transcribe its slots 3..10: they decide what a double-click flag, a wheel delta and a modifier do.

description: [S7.2, kind `value`] No corpus record has Shift, Ctrl or Alt down at a key message: all 32,580 GetKeyState reads of WM_KEYDOWN / WM_KEYUP return 0. uiKeyEvent 0x00495910 ORs 0x10000 / 0x20000 / 0x40000 into the code it hands the focus owner (0x00495925, 0x00495934, 0x00495943), and rootWin_onKey tests `code == 0x1000d` (0x0046577b), a code with the Shift bit. The translator passes the plain virtual key as `code` (a1 of handler 7, a0 of handler 8) with no modifier bits, so that branch of rootWin_onKey cannot be reached from it and a shifted key may need the bits ORed in. Where the bits enter (listener slot 3 / 4 or the exe's pump) is not established.
path to resolution: Record a key sweep with Shift / Ctrl held (a scenario that posts WM_KEYDOWN with the virtual key state forced through SimGolfShim_SetVirtualKey) and read the HANDLER a0 / a1; or transcribe the listener (U-1610).

description: [S7.2, kind `scope`] Display::createWindow registers the window class with style 0x2b (re/match/jgld_display.cpp line 114: CS_VREDRAW | CS_HREDRAW | CS_DBLCLKS | CS_OWNDC), so a real fast second click arrives as WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK / WM_RBUTTONDBLCLK, which windowProc hands to slots 7 / 9 with the flag 1 (0x1006965f, 0x100696e6); the harness never posts those (the corpus holds only 0x100..0x102, 0x200, 0x201, 0x202, 0x204, 0x205). The translator treats the double-click message as the press (handler 2 / 5) and reports Evidence::Unmeasured. What the listener does with the flag is not known.
path to resolution: Same as U-1610, or a recorded double-click (post WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK through the harness) and the HANDLER records after it.

description: [S7.2, kind `scope`] WM_MOUSEWHEEL (slot 6 with HIWORD(wParam)) and the middle button never occur in the corpus. The translator yields no steps for them (Evidence::Unmeasured). Whether the game scrolls on the wheel is not known.

[S7.2, kind `scope`] WM_SYSKEYDOWN / WM_SYSKEYUP (Alt combinations): jgld's key handler onKey 0x10069c70 serves the four key messages alike (its Purpose, c3dg), so the translator maps them as 0x100 / 0x101 by that evidence; no corpus record contains one, and WM_SYSCHAR / WM_DEADCHAR / WM_SYSDEADCHAR are dropped without evidence.
path to resolution: Record Alt+key; or transcribe windowProc's arms for 0x103 / 0x106 / 0x107.

description: [S7.2, kind `field`] Command::t (the timeGetTime value the deadline tail of handlers 2, 3 and 7 compares with g_audio5aa774) is set from HostInput::now_ms() but not judged by the checker: the deadline word is 0 in every corpus run, so no CLOCKRUN lies in handler code.
path to resolution: A scenario that sets the deadline word; until then the host passes a live clock and the value is irrelevant.

description: [S7.2, kind `scope`] HostInput::focus_child_takes(msg, wp) is a callback the translator cannot answer itself: whether a focused child window takes a WM_KEYDOWN / WM_CHAR depends on the window tree (uiKeyEvent -> onCommand -> dispatchAccel, uiKeyEvent148 -> Window::onKeyChar). The checker answers it with parse_trace's rule (no HANDLER record follows), which judges the translator's use of the answer and not the answer; the live host must evaluate the same window-tree dispatch before the root handlers run. The corpus holds 25 focus-child keys, all in cov_r_bio (the character editor's bio entry).
path to resolution: S7.3 wires it to the port's window tree; today only chareditor.cpp's bio entry exists (U-1191).

description: [S7.2, kind `value`] MapVirtualKeyA(vk, MAPVK_VK_TO_CHAR) decides handler 8 (result != 0) or handler 7 (result 0) for a key-down. The corpus layout gives 187 -> 43 and 189 -> 45 (not the characters '=' and '-' of a US layout), so the answers depend on the keyboard layout of the recording PC, and the translator asks the host's live MapVirtualKeyA. A dead key sets bit 31 of the result: whether the original tests `!= 0` or the sign is not established (no corpus vk is a dead key).
path to resolution: Transcribe the MAPVK consumer (the caller of the MAPVK read: Window::dispatchAccel / the listener slot) and record a dead-key press.

description: [S7.2, kind `value`] A WM_CHAR's a0 is masked to its low byte (jgld onChar reads `byte ptr [ebp+0xc]`, 0x10069d6a). All 5,949 corpus WM_CHAR wParams are below 0x80 (largest 122), so the handling of an ANSI character 0x80..0xff (the window class is the A-class: 'n with tilde' = 0xf1) is not recorded: the sink may sign-extend the byte.
path to resolution: A recorded WM_CHAR 0xf1 and the HANDLER a0.

description: [S7.2, kind `scope`] Equivalent mutant on the corpus: the host-window scale / origin control (checker --negctl 10) reads GREEN on the identity viewport the traces were recorded with and RED only with --viewport; the corpus cannot judge the scaling, the --viewport mode (physical coordinates built as ceil(logical * client / 800) + origin, so each maps back exactly) does. Downscaled windows (client below 800x600) lose points by nature and are refused by the checker.
path to resolution: S7.3's live app_drive.py run through a scaled window.
